name: Digital 3D-printed ceramics
summary: Vessels that a machine builds layer by layer from a clay paste, after a digital model. The visible layer lines, the open lattice and the complex curves give the style its look.

philosophy.core_thesis: When a machine builds the form from a file, the vessel can have a shape that no wheel or mould can make, and the layer line becomes the ornament.
design_principles: Draw the form as a digital model with a parametric rule: a twist, a wave, a lattice or a gradient.
Print the clay paste in layers of 0.8 to 2 mm with a nozzle of 1 to 4 mm.
Keep the layer lines as the surface texture; do not sand them away.
Vary the wall in one piece: a solid base, a thin wall and an open lattice at the top.
Print porcelain or stoneware paste that holds its shape, and dry it slowly for 3 to 7 days.
Fire the piece in one cycle at 1220 to 1300 °C, with a support of kiln setters where it overhangs.
Use a thin satin or clear glaze that keeps the ridges, or leave the surface bare.
Print a colour pattern with a ceramic inkjet if the piece needs a graphic surface.
anti_patterns: A smooth, wheel-thrown surface with no layer line
A thick, glossy glaze that fills the ridges
A traditional folk or floral decoration
A form that a plain mould could make
A random mess of lines with no rule

form.shape: Vases, planters, lidded jars, bottle vases and sculptural vessels with twisted, ribbed, lattice or gradient walls.
form.profile: A smooth, complex curve that is built from fine rings: twisted columns, wave walls, open lace and thin double walls.
form.foot_and_rim: A flat printed base that is part of the first layers; the rim is a clean horizontal cut or a lattice edge.
form.proportion: Height 10 to 60 cm; wall 1 to 4 mm, and a lattice with openings of 3 to 15 mm.
rules: Make the form follow a digital rule that the viewer can read.
Keep the layer lines at one regular pitch.
Design the overhangs to be less than 45 degrees, or add a support.

bodies.rule: Use a smooth paste that flows through a nozzle and then holds its shape. Paper clay and fine porcelain are the best at thin walls and overhangs.

methods: 3D printing of clay paste with a screw extruder
slow drying on a plaster bed
forming.joins: The vessel is printed in one piece, with no joins; lids and parts are printed separately and fitted by the file.
forming.details: Regular layer lines, a small seam where each layer starts, precise lattice openings and a flat, exact base.

glaze.pattern: Fine, regular horizontal ridges that run round the form; a twisted rib; a lattice wall; a colour gradient that is printed in ceramic ink.
glaze.gloss: Matt to satin, 5 to 50 GU; thin glaze keeps the ridges sharp.
glaze.wear: The ridges collect dust and are harder to clean; the thin lattice is brittle, and a thin wall chips at the rim.

palette.strategy: A restrained, clean palette that makes the form the main subject: white, pale grey and clay, with an occasional strong colour.

firing.kiln: An electric kiln, with a slow, even oxidation firing.
processes: digital modelling and slicing of the file
printing of the clay paste in layers
firing.scale: One piece takes 2 to 20 hours to print; a studio prints one to a few pieces each day.
firing.signs: Regular layer lines, a faint seam where the layers start, and a clean, exact lattice.

pieces.form: Tall vase of printed porcelain with a twisted rib and visible layer lines
Round planter with a wave wall of porcelain stoneware and a matt glaze
Open lattice vessel of paper clay, left bare
Bottle vase with a gradient pattern in printed ceramic ink
Jar with a printed lid that fits with a 0.3 mm gap

evidence.title: Ceramic 3D printing by Studio Under, detail

emotion.target_response: A feeling of calm precision and surprise: the viewer sees an exact, complex form and wonders how it was made.

use_cases: a parametric vase or lamp shade for a modern interior
a museum label on digital ceramics
avoid_when: the brief needs a hand-thrown irregular pot
the brief needs a thick glaze effect
the brief needs a traditional decoration

modifiers.how: Replace the machine layers with throwing rings, and use a thick ash or kaki glaze.
Keep the form simple and add a bold printed pattern in flat colour.

wall_thickness.note: Printed walls can be very thin, but a lattice needs a minimum of 1 mm.
